title: How to turn release notes into product launch videos
summary: Your release notes are already the script. Here's how to turn it into a 60-second product launch video for social, email, and in-app — without a video team.
body_markdown:
Your product ships something new every couple of weeks, and almost none of it gets a video. The release note goes out, maybe a[changelog entry](https://www.clueso.io/blog/release-note-videos-vs-changelogs) , maybe a line in the newsletter, and the work of turning that into something people actually watch never happens because it means starting from a blank timeline every single time. So the launches that deserve a moment get a paragraph instead — and[sales never gets what it needs to sell what you just shipped](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-to-enable-sales-to-sell-what-you-just-shipped) .


That's a workflow problem, not a creativity problem. The raw material already exists the day you ship: the release note or the Jira ticket describes what changed, who it's for, and why it matters. The job is turning that write-up into a video without rebuilding the whole thing by hand.


## What is a product launch video?


A product launch video is a short video, usually 30 to 90 seconds, that announces a new feature, update, or release. It's built to travel across a LinkedIn post, a release email, or an in-app banner, and its job is to make people notice and understand what changed, not to teach every step of using it. That last part matters for how you make it.


Most teams conflate this with a product demo. A[demo](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-demo-video-archetypes) walks through the feature in the product itself and answers "how do I use this." A launch video answers "what's new and should I care." Different question, different format, and usually a different production method.


## Why release notes are the right starting point


The release note already contains the four things a launch script needs: what shipped, who it helps, the problem it solves, and what to do next. You wrote that down for the changelog anyway. Reusing it means the marketing artifact and the product truth stay in sync, instead of a copywriter three days later guessing at what the engineers built.


Consider a mid-size B2B team shipping a new bulk-export feature. The Jira ticket has the summary ("export up to 50,000 rows to CSV in one click"), the acceptance criteria, and screenshots the QA engineer attached. That's a script outline and a shot list sitting in one place. The work left is trimming it to a spoken 45 seconds and choosing which two screenshots carry the story.


Pulling from the ticket also means the video can be triggered by the release itself. When a ticket moves to "shipped" or a release note publishes, that's the signal to draft the video, using the same source of truth the rest of the launch runs on.

## When a motion-graphic launch video beats a screen recording


Here's the call most teams get wrong. For a feature announcement going into a newsletter or a social feed, a screen recording is often the worse choice. Recordings are longer, they show UI that doesn't compress well into a 30-second clip, and they assume the viewer has sound on and context loaded. A[motion-graphic video](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) — clean screenshots, big[text callouts](https://www.clueso.io/tools/text-animation) , a tight[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) — reads in three seconds on a muted autoplay and holds up at thumbnail size.


You should use a[screen recording](https://www.clueso.io/features/screen-recorder) when the point is "how this works" and the viewer has already opted in: a[help center article](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) , an onboarding email, a deep-dive[walkthrough](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-walkthrough-videos) . On the other hand, use a motion-graphic launch video when the point is "this exists and it's good," and you're competing for attention in a feed. The table below is to help you understand when to build what:


Situation Motion-graphic launch video Screen recording


Social post / LinkedIn / X Strong fit — short, reads on mute Weak — too long, needs sound


Release newsletter Strong fit — hype plus clarity Situational — only for a headline feature


In-app "what's new" banner Strong fit — quick, on-brand Situational


Help center / how-to Weak — skips the actual steps Strong fit — shows the real workflow


Sales deep-dive demo Weak — too shallow Strong fit — full walkthrough


The animated format has a second advantage. You don't need a clean, bug-free build in a demo environment to record against. Screenshots from the Jira ticket are enough, which means you can cut the video the day of launch instead of waiting for a stable staging instance.

## A repeatable workflow: release write-up to video


The point of a workflow is that it runs the same way every time, so the decision "does this ship get a video" stops being a debate. Here's the version that would hold up across a busy release calendar.


1. **Start from the release note or Jira ticket.** Grab the summary, the customer-facing benefit, and any screenshots already attached. Don't rewrite from scratch — edit down what's there.
2. **Cut a 45-to-75-second script.** One hook line, one or two benefit lines, one line on what changed visually, one close with the next step. Read it out loud; if it runs past 90 seconds spoken, cut it.
3. **Choose two or three visuals.** For a launch video, a screenshot of the new UI with a text callout beats a full recording. Pick the frames that show the change, not the whole app.
4. **Generate the video with narration.** Turn the script and screenshots into a motion-graphic video with an AI voiceover, so you're not booking a recording session for a 45-second clip.
5. **Publish to the channels that already exist.** The release email, the social post, the in-app banner. Same asset, resized where needed — we break down[where to announce SaaS product updates](https://www.clueso.io/blog/announce-saas-product-updates) channel by channel.


Clueso can take a release write-up and a few screenshots and produce a motion-graphic launch video with an AI voiceover, and it can pull the source material from tools like Jira through its integrations, so the video draft starts from the ticket instead of a blank page. The pillar here is speed without a video team: a[product marketer](https://www.clueso.io/blog/videos-for-product-marketing-teams) can ship the launch video the same afternoon the feature goes live, without waiting on editing or a recording booth.


The workflow also compounds. Once the first three launch videos share a look — same intro frame, same caption style, same voiceover — the fourth one is mostly assembly.

## What to keep consistent across every launch video


Consistency is what makes a stream of launch videos feel like a product with momentum instead of a pile of one-offs. Lock a short intro, a[caption](https://www.clueso.io/features/video-captions) font and color, and one voiceover style, then reuse them. The viewer starts to recognize your releases on sight, and you stop making design decisions on every ship.


Keep the length honest too. A launch video that runs past 90 seconds is a demo wearing the wrong clothes. If the feature genuinely needs a two-minute walkthrough, make that separately as a screen recording for the help center, and keep the launch video short.


## Where to start this week


Pick your next release. Open the ticket, cut the summary down to a 60-second script, grab two screenshots that show the change, and produce one motion-graphic launch video before the release note goes out. Ship it in the release email. Do the same on the next release, and the one after, until "every ship gets a video" is just how the release process works.


## Frequently asked questions


**How long should a product launch video be?**


For social and newsletter use, aim for 30 to 75 seconds. Anything past 90 seconds is usually a demo, and demos belong in the help center or a sales call, not a feed competing for a three-second glance.


**Can I turn a Jira ticket directly into a video?**


Yes. The ticket's summary and acceptance criteria give you the script outline, and any attached screenshots give you the shots. A platform that connects to Jira can pull that source in so you edit rather than start blank.


**Should a launch video be a screen recording or a motion-graphic video?**


For announcements, use a motion-graphic video — it's shorter, reads on mute, and doesn't need a polished live build. Save screen recordings for how-to content where the viewer wants to follow the actual steps.


**How do we make sure every release gets a video?**


Tie the video to a trigger you already have, like a ticket moving to "shipped" or a release note publishing. When the video is a step in the release process instead of a separate project, it stops getting skipped.
